declarations.description:
Every user-facing string Peacock renders on its own: labels for icon buttons, screen-reader text,
empty states, toolbar names. Apps translate them once with `setPeacockStrings()`; components that
render many strings also take a per-instance `strings` property. A string with values is a function.

Numbers and dates are formatted with `Intl` in the resolved locale, never here.

declarations.name: setPeacockStrings
declarations.description:
Replaces Peacock's strings, for example with a translation. Entries left out keep their English
default. Every connected component re-renders with the new strings.

declarations.name: peacockString
declarations.description: The current value of one string.

declarations.name: onPeacockStringsChange
declarations.description: Calls the listener whenever the strings change; returns a function that stops listening.

declarations.name: setIconBase
declarations.description:
Loads a provider's icons from `base`, a folder holding `<name>.svg`, instead of cdn.jsdelivr.net:
for pages that must not leave their own origin, such as an intranet or a page whose content
security policy allows only `connect-src 'self'`. A relative `base` resolves against the page.
`loader-full.js` does this for Material Symbols with the icons it ships in `icons/`.

declarations.name: IndividualComponent
declarations.description:
Build marker, not a runtime decorator: it does nothing when the class is defined.

`rollup.config.js` scans `src/` for `@IndividualComponent` and gives every marked class its own
entry file in `dist/` (for example `dist/button.js`), which the loader imports lazily the first
time the tag appears on the page. Mark every public component class with it; leave it off
internal building blocks that should only ship inside another component's bundle.

declarations.name: dispatchActivationClick
declarations.description:
Dispatches a click event to the given element that triggers a native action,
but is not composed and therefore is not seen outside the element.

This is useful for responding to an external click event on the host element
that should trigger an internal action like a button click.

Note, a helper is provided because setting this up correctly is a bit tricky.
In particular, calling `click` on an element creates a composed event, which
is not desirable, and a manually dispatched event must specifically be a
`MouseEvent` to trigger a native action.

declarations.name: isActivationClick
declarations.description:
Returns true if the click event should trigger an activation behavior. The
behavior is defined by the element and is whatever it should do when
clicked.

Typically when an element needs to handle a click, the click is generated
from within the element and an event listener within the element implements
the needed behavior; however, it's possible to fire a click directly
at the element that the element should handle. This method helps
distinguish these "external" clicks.

An "external" click can be triggered in a number of ways: via a click
on an associated label for a form  associated element, calling
`element.click()`, or calling
`element.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', ...))`.

Also works around Firefox issue
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1804576 by squelching
events for a microtask after called.

Add a hook for an event that is called after the event is dispatched and

declarations.name: nativeValidity
declarations.description: The validity of a native control, for controls that wrap one.

Base class for Peacock's form controls.

It is form-associated: `value` is submitted with the surrounding `<form>`, `form.reset()`
restores the value the control started with, and a disabled `<fieldset>` disables it.
`name` and `disabled` come from `mixinFormAssociated`; they are backed by attributes, so
subclasses must not redeclare them.

It takes part in constraint validation like a native control: `required` and the control's own
rules (from `computeValidity()`) block form submission, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity()`, `validity` and `validationMessage` work as on `<input>`, and `:invalid`
matches. A control shows its message (`validationText`) once the person has committed a value
or the form was submitted.

It can hold a value the assistant suggested (ADR-030002): `suggestion` fills the control and
marks it until the person accepts or clears it. `sensitive` keeps the control out of AI
altogether. Subclasses show the marker with `suggestionBadge()` and `suggestionReason`, and
override `readSuggestionValue()`, `writeSuggestionValue()` and `emitSuggestionValue()` when
their value is not `value` with `input`/`change` events.

declarations.description:
Shared behaviour for Peacock overlays (modal, side and bottom sheets, popover, tooltip,
snackbar): the top layer, so overlays stack in the order they open and never sit under an
open modal; a ref-counted page scroll lock for modal overlays; Escape and light dismiss that
close only the topmost overlay; initial focus and focus return.

The host keeps `open` as the source of truth: it calls `sync(open)` from `updated()`, and the
controller calls `requestClose(reason)` when the user asks to close. The host then sets
`open = false` and fires its `close` event with that reason.

declarations.description:
The menu wiring shared by buttons that open a `wc-menu` (dropdown button, split button):
show / close / toggle, Arrow Up / Down on the trigger, the trigger's `aria-haspopup`,
`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the host's `open` / `close` events (ADR-030001).

The menu's own `open` / `close` events are stopped inside the host, which fires its own `open`
and `close` instead; `close` carries `detail.reason` from the menu's close event. The host renders the menu with `id=${trigger.menuId}`, `@open=${trigger.handleMenuOpen}`
and `@close=${trigger.handleMenuClose}`, and the trigger button with
`.configAria=${trigger.triggerAria}`, `@click=${trigger.handleTriggerClick}` and
`@keydown=${trigger.handleTriggerKeyDown}`.

The URL that the hyperlink points to. When set, the component renders as an `<a>` element.
Maps to the native `href` attribute.

members.name: target
members.description:
Where to display the linked URL. Maps to the native `target` attribute.
Possible values are `"_self"`, `"_blank"`, `"_parent"`, `"_top"`, or a custom frame name.
When using `"_blank"`, consider setting `rel="noopener noreferrer"` for security. Defaults to `"_self"`.

members.name: rel
members.description:
The relationship between the current document and the linked URL.
Maps to the native `rel` attribute on the rendered `<a>` element.
When `target="_blank"`, use `"noopener noreferrer"` to prevent tab-napping attacks.

members.name: download

members.description:
When true, the skeleton animation is shown. A skeleton is the placeholder look of content
that has not arrived yet, not a busy state: components that are working on something use
`loading` (ADR-030001), and `skeleton` on a component (chip, list item, button) asks for
this placeholder look.

declarations.description:
Base class for Peacock's text-like fields (input, textarea, number, URL, select, date/time,
color). It adds the props every field shares (label, helper/error/warning text, variant, size,
clearable, `start`/`end` slots) and renders the `wc-field` frame.

It also makes the inner control accessible across the shadow boundary: `fieldAria()` gives it
an accessible name from `label`, `aria-invalid` while an error shows, and `aria-describedby`
pointing at a hidden copy of the helper or error text in the same shadow root.

Subclasses call `renderField(control, options)` in `render()`, spread `fieldAria()` onto the
native control, call `emitValue('input' | 'change')` instead of re-dispatching native events
(the field event contract: `CustomEvent<{ value }>`, bubbling and composed), and override
`clearValue()` if clearing means more than `value = ''`.

members.description: Disables the control: it can't be focused or changed, and its value isn't submitted.

members.description: Shows the value but stops the user changing it; unlike `disabled`, it stays focusable and is submitted.

members.description:

members.description:
A value the assistant suggests, with why. The control takes the value and shows a Suggested
badge and the reason until the person edits it, the form is submitted, or the badge clears it,

members.description: Why the value was suggested, while the suggestion shows; else `''`.

members.description: Pushes the current validity to `ElementInternals`.

members.name: __observeInputBox
members.description:

control's text and floats into the outline's notch; the text's start moves with leading

The outline. The outlined variant builds it from parts, as Material 3 does: a start segment,
a notch as wide as the floating label whose top edge opens while the label floats, and an
end segment that takes the remaining width. The label floats into the notch, so the
outline needs no background behind the label and works on any surface.

declarations.description:
Base for text fields that open a picker in a popover: `wc-date-field`, `wc-time-field` and
`wc-datetime-field`.

The field keeps the typed text in `draft` and parses it on blur or Enter. Valid text becomes
`value` (always ISO, so forms submit a locale-independent value) and fires `change`; text that
does not parse, or falls outside `min`/`max`, keeps the draft, shows an error and makes the
field invalid (`badInput`, `rangeUnderflow` or `rangeOverflow`). Values picked in the popover
fire `input` while they change and `change` once committed.

Subclasses supply the parsing, formatting, validation and the picker itself.

declarations.description:
Ghost text for a native textarea (ADR-030002): after a pause in typing at the end of a line, the
provider's `complete` suggests how to go on, shown in grey after the caret. Tab takes it, Mod+→
takes the next word, Escape or any other key dismisses it. Nothing is inserted until the person
takes it.

The suggestion is drawn in a mirror laid over the control, with the control's text metrics, so
it wraps like real text. Screen readers get it through the control's description.

Usage: wrap the control in an element with `position: relative`, render `render()` beside it,
call `onInput()` from the control's `input`, `onKeyDown()` from its `keydown`, and `clear()` on
blur, scroll and selection changes; spread `describedBy()` into its `aria-describedby`.
declarations.name: GhostTextController

members.name: available
members.description: Whether ghost text can be offered now.

members.name: text
members.description: The suggestion shown, or `''`.

members.name: describedBy
members.description: The id to add to the control's `aria-describedby` while a suggestion shows.

members.name: onInput
members.description: The person typed: drop the suggestion and ask again after a pause.

members.name: onKeyDown
members.description: Tab takes the suggestion, Mod+→ a word, Escape dismisses; other keys dismiss it too.

members.name: clear
members.description: Drops the suggestion and any request for it.

declarations.description:
Base for Peacock's on/off controls: `wc-checkbox`, `wc-switch` and `wc-radio`.

Like a native checkbox, `checked` is the state and `value` the string submitted under `name`
while checked (`"on"` by default). `required` blocks form submission until the control is
checked. The inner control (an element with class `container` and a `role`) gets the host's
`tabindex` and `aria-*`, and is named by the visible label through `aria-labelledby`.

Subclasses render the control with `controlAttributes()`, the label with `renderLabel()`, and
call `toggleChecked(event)` (or their own selection logic) on activation.

its name, required and invalid state, plus `configAria`.

members.description: Flips `checked` and fires `change`, unless the control is disabled or read-only.

members.name: dispatchChange
members.description:
Fires `change`. `detail.checked` is the new state and `detail.value` the submitted value
while checked.

members.name: renderLabel
members.description:
The visible label, from `label` or the default slot, with the id that names the control, and
the Suggested badge after it while a suggestion shows.

members.name: readSuggestionValue
members.description: A suggestion for a toggle is its `checked` state.

members.name: writeSuggestionValue
members.description: Puts a suggested or restored value into the control.

members.name: emitSuggestionValue
members.description: Fires `input` and `change` after the person cleared a suggestion.

members.name: hostClick
members.description:
A click aimed at the host itself, not at something inside it, comes from an external
`<label for>`, a wrapping `<label>` or `host.click()`. Forward it to the inner native input, the
control the shadow `<label>` activates, so it toggles like a click on the control. Clicks from
inside (the control, the shadow label or slotted label content) start elsewhere and are left
alone, so a click toggles once.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control: it can't be focused or changed, and its value isn't submitted.

members.name: readonly
members.description: Shows the value but stops the user changing it; unlike `disabled`, it stays focusable and is submitted.

members.name: required
members.description: Requires a value before the form can submit.

members.name: skeleton
members.description: Shows a loading placeholder in place of the control.

members.name: sensitive
members.description:
Holds data that must never reach a model, such as a salary or a bank account: the control
takes no suggestions and offers no AI features.

members.name: suggestion
members.description:
A value the assistant suggests, with why. The control takes the value and shows a Suggested
badge and the reason until the person edits it, the form is submitted, or the badge clears it,
which puts the previous value back. `null` drops the marker and keeps the value. Ignored while
AI is off and on `sensitive` controls.

members.name: acceptSuggestion

members.name: dismissSuggestion
members.description: Clears the suggestion and puts the previous value back. Fires `dismiss`, `input` and `change`.

members.name: suggestionBadge
members.description:
The Suggested badge with its clear button, while a suggestion shows; else nothing. Controls
without helper text pass `withReason` so the badge's tooltip carries the reason.

outside the label element, so it is not part of the group's accessible name. Style
`.label-row` as a row.

declarations.summary: A code editor built on Monaco, with syntax highlighting, completions and debugging marks.

declarations.name: validMentions
declarations.description:
Keeps the mentions that still match the text: in range, not overlapping, and with the trigger
and label at their place. Sorted by position; each a copy.

declarations.name: shiftMentions
declarations.description:
Moves the mentions to follow an edit from `before` to `after`. A mention before the edit
stays, one after it moves by the change in length, and one the edit touched is dropped: its
text stays as typed, as plain text. `caret` is the caret after the edit; it places an edit
between repeated characters (typing `@` in front of `@Ana`).

declarations.name: findQuery
declarations.description:
The mention query that ends at `caret`: a trigger at the start of the text or after a space,
followed by up to 50 characters on the same line, without a leading space or two spaces in a
row (names have spaces; sentences have more). Nothing inside an existing mention counts.

declarations.name: editScript
declarations.description:
Myers' shortest edit script between `a` and `b`, or `null` when it needs more than `maxD`
edits. Space is O(D²) for the trace, time O((N + M) · D).

declarations.name: splitText
declarations.description: Splits on CRLF, LF and CR; a final line break does not start an empty last line.

declarations.name: wordDiff
declarations.description:
Word-level runs for a removed line and the added line it pairs with, or `null` when the lines
are too long or too different for word marks to help.

declarations.name: diffTexts
declarations.description: Diffs two texts line by line, with word marks on changed line pairs.

declarations.name: sparkle
declarations.description:
The sparkle that marks AI in Peacock. Material Symbols (0.40) has no sparkle glyph, so Peacock
ships its own. It is decorative: the text next to it says what it means.

declarations.name: readStream
declarations.description:
Reads a text stream into one growing string. `onText` gets the whole text so far at most once a
frame, so a fast stream causes one render per frame rather than one per chunk, and once more with
`done` at the end. Stops early when `signal` aborts. Resolves with the whole text.

declarations.description:
Model text as editor content, never parsed as HTML or Markdown (ADR-030002: model text is
untrusted): paragraphs split on blank lines, single line breaks kept as spaces. The first
paragraph is inline, so it joins the paragraph it is inserted into.

declarations.name: inlineDiff
declarations.description:
The changes from `before` to `after`, word by word, as one interleaved sequence for reading in
place: deletions next to the insertions that replace them. Falls back to "all deleted, all
inserted" when the texts are too different to align.

The AI layer of Peacock's rich-text editors (ADR-030002): ghost text after a pause in typing,
actions on the selection (Improve, Shorten, Fix, Translate, Tell it what to change) from the
selection bubble or the toolbar, and Continue writing and Summarize above in the slash menu.

Nothing the model writes reaches the document until the person takes it: ghost text needs Tab,
and an action's result streams into a preview panel with Accept, Discard and Try again, and a
Changes view for rewrites. The editor stays editable meanwhile; the range the result will
replace follows edits.

Every feature is offered only while the provider has it, AI is on, and the host is neither
`no-ai` nor `sensitive`.

fires `search {trigger, query}`, the app sets `suggestions` (and `suggestions-loading` while it

declarations.description:
The shared base of Peacock's rich-text fields (`wc-markdown-editor`, `wc-html-editor`,
`wc-comment-composer`): a form-associated Tiptap editor inside `wc-field`, with a fixed toolbar,
a selection bubble, a slash menu, a link editor, a block handle, mentions and a source view.

Subclasses say what the value is: the editor `profile`, how to read the value from the editor and
write it back, and the source language. Everything else, including the events, is here:
- `input` with `{ value }`, `debounce` milliseconds after the content stops changing;
- `change` with `{ value }` when focus leaves after an edit;
- `search` and `mention`, as on `wc-mention-input`.

With a provider that offers them (ADR-030002), the editors also get AI actions on the selection
(from the bubble and the toolbar), Continue writing and Summarize above in the slash menu, and,
with `ai-completion`, ghost text. Results show in a preview until the person accepts them.

declarations.description: The marked tokenizer for mention links; it runs before marked's own link tokenizer.

declarations.description: Splits Markdown into block tokens.

declarations.name: extractMentions
declarations.description:
The mentions in some Markdown, in document order, without duplicates (same trigger and id). Use

declarations.name: closeOpenMarkdown
declarations.description:
Makes the unfinished end of a streaming answer render as it will once complete, instead of
flashing raw Markdown: an open `**`, `~~` or `` ` `` is closed, and a link still being written
(`[label](addr`) is held back until its `)` arrives. Only the last block is touched, and nothing
inside an open code fence, which marked already shows as code to the end.

Only for display while streaming; the finished text is always rendered as it is.

Lexes Markdown that grows at the end, as a streamed answer does. While the new text extends the
previous one, the blocks before the last two are kept and only the end is lexed again, so a long
answer costs the same per chunk as a short one. Anything else is lexed in full.

declarations.name: printPages
declarations.description:
Prints the editor's pages as they are on screen. The caller lays them out without gaps first,
so each page fills one printed sheet exactly: the header, footer, page numbers and page breaks
print as they look.

The copy is put in a temporary shadow root in the same document, which shares the editor's
stylesheets and the page's theme tokens, so it lays out exactly like the screen; a print-only
stylesheet hides the rest of the page while the browser prints.

badge and the reason until the person edits it, the form is submitted, or the badge clears it,

declarations.name: getPageItems
declarations.description:
Builds the page list shown by the `full` pagination variant.

The list always keeps the first and last page, the current page and `siblings` pages on each
side of it, and fills the rest with an ellipsis. It never holds more than
`2 * siblings + 5` slots, so the control keeps its width while the user moves through pages.

Keys of the selected rows. Keys are compared as strings, so a numeric `id` of `1` matches

and are skipped by select-all.

members.name: managed
members.description:

`data` as given and only reports `sort` and page changes.

members.name: sortable
members.description: If true, columns are sortable. Defaults to `true`.

members.name: sortBy
members.description: The field name currently used for sorting (the primary sort).

members.name: sortOrder
members.description: The current sort order. Possible values are `"asc"` and `"desc"`. Defaults to `"asc"`.

members.name: sorts
members.description:
Every sort level, primary first, as `{ name, order }`. Shift+click on a header adds a level.
Kept in step with `sort-by` and `sort-order`, which describe the first level.

members.name: resizable
members.description:
Lets the user resize columns by dragging the header edges or with the arrow keys on the
focused handle. A column's own `resizable` overrides it.

members.name: reorderable
members.description:
Lets the user move columns by dragging a header or with Alt+Left/Right. Pinned columns move
only among the columns pinned to the same edge. A column's own `reorderable` overrides it.

members.name: columnMenu
members.description: Adds a column menu button at the end of the header that shows or hides columns.

members.name: page
members.description: The current page number (1-based). Defaults to `1`. Follows a slotted `wc-pagination`.

members.name: pageSize
members.description: The number of rows per page. Defaults to `10`. Follows a slotted `wc-pagination`.

members.description: Row height: `compact`, `default` or `comfortable`. Defaults to `default`.

members.name: striped
members.description: Shades every other row.

members.name: loading
members.description:
Shows a loading state: skeleton rows while there is no data, otherwise a progress bar
under the header so the current rows stay readable.

members.name: error
members.description: Shows an error in place of the rows, for example when loading failed. Announced politely.

members.name: errorText
members.description: Text of the error state. Defaults to Peacock's `tableErrorDescription` string.

members.name: label
members.description: Accessible name of the table.

members.name: emptyStateHeadline
members.description:
Headline text shown when the table has no data. Defaults to Peacock's `noItems` string
(`"No items"`).

members.name: emptyStateDescription
members.description:
Description text shown when the table has no data. Defaults to Peacock's
`noItemsDescription` string (`"There are no items to display"`).

members.name: detailTemplate
members.description:

expander buttons. A string is shown as text. Turns `virtual` off: detail rows vary in height.

members.name: expandedRowKeys
members.description: Keys of the rows whose details are shown. Keys are compared as strings.

members.name: groupBy
members.description:
Groups the rows by this field under collapsible header rows. Groups are ordered by value
(descending when the table is sorted descending by this field); sorting applies within
groups. In managed mode, groups keep the order the rows come in.

members.name: collapsedGroups

attributes.name: columns
attributes.description:
Grid columns configuration. Each column can have: name, label, width, minWidth, maxWidth
and flex (rem and grow factor), fixed, align, type, sortable, wrap, hidden, hideable,
resizable, reorderable, group, headerTemplate, template; editable, editor, options,
required, min, max, step and validate for inline editing; exportValue; aggregate.

attributes.name: data
attributes.description: Grid data to display on table.

attributes.name: selection
attributes.description:
How rows are selected: `none` (default), `single` (one row, with radio buttons) or
`multiple` (checkboxes, a select-all checkbox and the selection bar).

attributes.name: selected-row-keys
attributes.description:
Keys of the selected rows. Keys are compared as strings, so a numeric `id` of `1` matches
`"1"`.

attributes.name: key-field
attributes.description: The field name used as the unique key for each row. Defaults to `"id"`.

attributes.name: managed
attributes.description:
If true, sorting and pagination are managed externally (controlled mode): the table shows
`data` as given and only reports `sort` and page changes.

attributes.name: sortable
attributes.description: If true, columns are sortable. Defaults to `true`.

attributes.name: sort-by
attributes.description: The field name currently used for sorting (the primary sort).

attributes.name: sort-order
attributes.description: The current sort order. Possible values are `"asc"` and `"desc"`. Defaults to `"asc"`.

attributes.name: sorts
attributes.description:
Every sort level, primary first, as `{ name, order }`. Shift+click on a header adds a level.
Kept in step with `sort-by` and `sort-order`, which describe the first level.

attributes.name: resizable
attributes.description:
Lets the user resize columns by dragging the header edges or with the arrow keys on the
focused handle. A column's own `resizable` overrides it.

attributes.name: reorderable
attributes.description:
Lets the user move columns by dragging a header or with Alt+Left/Right. Pinned columns move
only among the columns pinned to the same edge. A column's own `reorderable` overrides it.

attributes.name: column-menu
attributes.description: Adds a column menu button at the end of the header that shows or hides columns.

attributes.name: page
attributes.description: The current page number (1-based). Defaults to `1`. Follows a slotted `wc-pagination`.

attributes.name: page-size
attributes.description: The number of rows per page. Defaults to `10`. Follows a slotted `wc-pagination`.

attributes.name: density
attributes.description: Row height: `compact`, `default` or `comfortable`. Defaults to `default`.

attributes.name: striped
attributes.description: Shades every other row.

attributes.name: loading
attributes.description:
Shows a loading state: skeleton rows while there is no data, otherwise a progress bar
under the header so the current rows stay readable.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Shows an error in place of the rows, for example when loading failed. Announced politely.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Text of the error state. Defaults to Peacock's `tableErrorDescription` string.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name of the table.

attributes.name: empty-state-headline
attributes.description:
Headline text shown when the table has no data. Defaults to Peacock's `noItems` string
(`"No items"`).

attributes.name: empty-state-description
attributes.description:
Description text shown when the table has no data. Defaults to Peacock's
`noItemsDescription` string (`"There are no items to display"`).

attributes.name: expanded-row-keys
attributes.description: Keys of the rows whose details are shown. Keys are compared as strings.

attributes.name: group-by
attributes.description:
Groups the rows by this field under collapsible header rows. Groups are ordered by value
(descending when the table is sorted descending by this field); sorting applies within
groups. In managed mode, groups keep the order the rows come in.

attributes.name: collapsed-groups
attributes.description: Keys of the collapsed groups: their `group-by` values as strings (`""` for empty values).

attributes.name: virtual
attributes.description:
Renders only the rows in view (plus a few on each side), for large `data` without
pagination. Every row must have the same height, `--table-row-height`; cells do not wrap.
Give the table a height. Has no effect with `detailTemplate`.

attributes.description: Rows the footer aggregates cover: `all` rows (default) or the current `page`.

members.description:
Dims the card and makes its content inert. An actionable or link card also stops responding
to clicks and leaves the tab order, unless `disabled-reason` is set.

members.description:

Possible values are `"_self"`, `"_blank"`, `"_parent"`, `"_top"`, or a custom frame name.
When using `"_blank"`, consider setting `rel="noopener noreferrer"` for security. Defaults to `"_self"`.

members.name: rel
members.description:

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: When `true`, the button is disabled and cannot be interacted with. Reflects to the `disabled` attribute. Defaults to `false`.

attributes.name: soft-disabled
attributes.description:
When `true`, the button is visually styled as disabled and cannot be interacted with, but remains focusable.

Rendered as a visually hidden tooltip and linked via `aria-describedby` for accessibility.

attributes.name: href

attributes.name: target
attributes.description:

frame name. Pair `"_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

attributes.name: rel
attributes.description: The relationship of the linked URL to the current page, as the native `rel` attribute.

attributes.name: download
attributes.description:

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The value associated with this menu item, used to identify it on selection.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description:
What the item is. `"item"` (default) is an action; `"checkbox"` toggles `selected` and keeps
the menu open; `"radio"` selects this item and clears the other radio items of its group.
`"checkbox"` and `"radio"` expose `selected` as `aria-checked`.

attributes.name: selected

attributes.name: current

attributes.name: keep-open

attributes.name: has-submenu

members.name: values

members.name: _handleMenuKeyDownCapture

members.description: With search, typing while an option has focus goes back to the input.

active-indicator pill with the label below it, the `active-icon` slot and a badge on the icon.

members.name: value
members.description:
The selected value. With `multiple`, a comma-separated list of values (use `values`), so
option values must not contain commas.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether the person can choose several options.

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name, when no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is set.

members.name: roving
members.default: new RovingFocusController(this, { items: () => this.options, orientation: () => 'vertical', typeahead: () => true, initialItem: items => items.find(option => (option as ListboxOption).selected) ?? items[0], isFocusable: item => !this.disabled && !(item as ListboxOption).disabled && !item.hidden, onMove: item => { if (!this.multiple) this.__choose(item as ListboxOption); }, })

members.name: options
members.description: The options, in order.

members.name: values
members.description:
The selected values, kept in sync with `value`. For a single listbox it holds at most one
value. The form gets one entry per value.

members.name: valueMissingText
members.description: The message for a missing required value.

members.name: validityAnchor
members.description: The element the browser points at when it reports a problem.

members.name: __syncOptions
members.description: Pushes `selected` and `multiple` onto the options, and moves the tab stop to a selection.

members.name: __interactive
members.description: Whether the person may change the selection now.

members.name: __choose
members.description: Single: makes `option` the value. Multiple: toggles it. Fires `change` when it changed.

members.name: __inOptionOrder
members.description: Values sorted in the order of their options, so `value` does not depend on click order.

members.name: name
members.description: The name the value is submitted under in a form.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables the control: it can't be focused or changed, and its value isn't submitted.

members.name: readonly
members.description: Shows the value but stops the user changing it; unlike `disabled`, it stays focusable and is submitted.

members.name: required
members.description: Requires a value before the form can submit.

members.name: skeleton
members.description: Shows a loading placeholder in place of the control.

members.name: sensitive
members.description:
Holds data that must never reach a model, such as a salary or a bank account: the control
takes no suggestions and offers no AI features.

members.name: suggestion
members.description:
A value the assistant suggests, with why. The control takes the value and shows a Suggested
badge and the reason until the person edits it, the form is submitted, or the badge clears it,
which puts the previous value back. `null` drops the marker and keeps the value. Ignored while
AI is off and on `sensitive` controls.

members.name: showValidity
members.description: Whether to show the validation message: after a commit, or after a failed submit.

members.name: __defaultValue
members.description: The value the control had when it was first connected; `form.reset()` returns to it.

members.name: __suggestions
members.default: new SuggestionController(this, { read: () => this.readSuggestionValue(), write: value => this.writeSuggestionValue(value), emit: () => this.emitSuggestionValue(), })

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description: Sets a custom error message, as on `<input>`; an empty string clears it.

members.name: suggested
members.description: Whether the control holds a suggestion the person hasn't accepted or cleared.

members.name: acceptSuggestion
members.description: Accepts the suggestion: the value stays and the marker goes. Fires `accept`.

members.name: dismissSuggestion
members.description: Clears the suggestion and puts the previous value back. Fires `dismiss`, `input` and `change`.

members.name: suggestionBadge
members.description:
The Suggested badge with its clear button, while a suggestion shows; else nothing. Controls
without helper text pass `withReason` so the badge's tooltip carries the reason.

members.name: labelWithSuggestion
members.description:
A group's label with the Suggested badge beside it while a suggestion shows. The badge stays
outside the label element, so it is not part of the group's accessible name. Style
`.label-row` as a row.

members.name: suggestionReason
members.description: Why the value was suggested, while the suggestion shows; else `''`.

members.name: suggestionVisible
members.description: Whether a suggestion shows as one now (AI on, not sensitive).

members.name: readSuggestionValue
members.description: The value a suggestion replaces and a dismissed one restores.

members.name: writeSuggestionValue
members.description: Puts a suggested or restored value into the control.

members.name: emitSuggestionValue
members.description: Fires `input` and `change` after the person cleared a suggestion.

members.name: computeValidity
members.description:
The control's own validity. The default checks `required` against an empty `value`;
controls that wrap a native input return `nativeValidity(input)`, others add their rules.

members.name: updateValidity
members.description: Pushes the current validity to `ElementInternals`.

members.name: validationText
members.description: The message to show under the control, or '' while there is nothing to show.

members.name: parseRestoreState
members.description: Turns saved form state back into a value. Strings by default.

declarations.name: SECOND
declarations.description:
Relative and absolute times ("5 minutes ago", "in 3 days", "Nov 2"), and one shared ticker that
keeps every relative time on the page current. Used by `wc-relative-time`, the discussion entries and
`wc-notification-center`.

declarations.name: parseDatetime
declarations.description: Parses an ISO 8601 date-time (or anything `Date` reads); `null` when it is not a date.

declarations.name: parseDuration
declarations.description:
Parses an ISO 8601 duration such as `P7D`, `PT12H` or `P1W` into milliseconds (months are 30.44
days, years 365.25); `null` when it is not a duration.

declarations.name: relativeTimeUnit
declarations.description:
The value and unit that describe a distance of `diff` milliseconds (negative is past): seconds
under 45 s, minutes under 45 min, hours under 22 h, days under 6.5 days, weeks under 26 days,
months under 320 days, then years. Under 45 s it is 0 seconds, which formats as "now".

declarations.name: formatRelativeTime
declarations.description: `date` relative to now in `locale`, such as "5 minutes ago", "in 3 days", "yesterday" or "now".

declarations.name: formatAbsoluteTime
declarations.description: `date` as an absolute date and time in `locale`, such as "Nov 7, 2026, 3:04 PM".

declarations.name: formatAbsoluteDate
declarations.description: `date` as a short date in `locale`: "Nov 2" in the current year, else "Nov 2, 2025".

declarations.name: formatTime
declarations.description:
`date` relative to now ("5 minutes ago"), or, when `absoluteAfter` is set and the date is
farther from now than that, an absolute date ("Nov 2").

declarations.name: refreshInterval
declarations.description:
How soon a relative time `diff` milliseconds from now may read differently: every 10 seconds
under a minute, every minute under an hour, every 5 minutes under a day, then every hour.

declarations.name: tickerRunning
declarations.description: Whether the shared ticker has a timer running. For tests.

declarations.name: onTick
declarations.description:
Calls `listener` again after `delay()` milliseconds (asked anew after each call), on one timer
shared by every subscriber on the page. The timer waits for the earliest subscriber, pauses
while the page is hidden, refreshes everyone when it is shown again, and stops when the last
subscriber leaves. Returns the unsubscribe function.

declarations.name: watchRelativeTime
declarations.description:
Calls `listener` whenever the relative time of `date()` may have changed: often for a time close
to now, rarely for one far away (see `refreshInterval`). A `null` date refreshes once a minute.
Returns the unsubscribe function.

declarations.description:
The deprecated name of the diagram canvas: `wc-flow` before 4.0, now `wc-diagram`. It works
like `wc-diagram` and warns once on the console. Removed in 5.0.

It has no tag in its JSDoc on purpose, so the custom elements manifest, the docs and the
React, Vue and Angular bindings list only `wc-diagram`. Its own module (`dist/flow.js`) keeps
the lazy loader's one-element-per-module rule.

declarations.name: GROUP_PADDING
declarations.description: Room a group box takes around its nodes, matching how the map draws groups.

declarations.name: forceLayout
declarations.description:
An organic layout: connected nodes attract, all nodes repel, nodes of a group drift together.
Starts from `previous` positions when given, so live updates are stable. Deterministic for the
same input (no random start).

declarations.name: layeredLayout
declarations.description:
A layered layout, upstream on the left and downstream on the right: each node goes one column
after its furthest caller, and nodes in a column are ordered to keep lines short (barycentre
sweeps). Cycles are broken at the edge that closes them.

declarations.name: radialLayout
declarations.description:
A radial layout around `center`: rings by the number of hops (either direction), with each
ring's nodes ordered to sit near the node that reached them. Unreached nodes go on an outer ring.

declarations.name: reachable
declarations.description: Ids reachable from `start` along edges: `upstream` follows edges backwards (who depends on it).

declarations.name: withinHops
declarations.description: Ids within `hops` steps of `start`, in either direction.

members.name: warnTaken
members.description:
Warns once that a tag is already defined by other code, such as a second copy or another
version of Peacock on the page. The existing definition stays; Peacock does not replace it.

members.name: start
members.description:
Defines the eager components and starts loading lazy ones as they appear.

By default it also wraps `Element.prototype.attachShadow` so components rendered inside any
shadow root load too. Pass `watchShadowRoots: false` (or load `loader.js?no-shadow-watch`) to
leave `attachShadow` alone, and call `loadComponents(shadowRoot)` for your own shadow roots.

members.name: watchShadowRoots
members.description:
Watches every shadow root attached from now on, as it is attached, so lazy components that a
component renders in its shadow root load as they do in the document. Patches
`attachShadow` once per page, even when two loaders run.

members.name: lazyLoadComponents
members.description: Loads the lazy components in `root` (a document or a shadow root) and those added later.

declarations.name: loadComponents
declarations.description:
Loads the Peacock components in `root` (a shadow root, element or document) and those added to
it later. Only needed with `loader.js?no-shadow-watch`.

Shared props and rendering for Peacock's text-like fields (input, textarea, number, URL, select,
date/time, color): label, helper/error/warning text, variant, size, clearable, `start`/`end`
slots and the `wc-field` frame.

It also makes the inner control accessible across the shadow boundary: `fieldAria()` gives it
an accessible name from `label`, `aria-invalid` while an error shows, and `aria-describedby`
pointing at a hidden copy of the helper or error text that lives in the same shadow root.

Components call `renderField(control, options)` in `render()`, spread `fieldAria()` onto the
native control, call `emitValue('input' | 'change')` instead of re-dispatching native events,
and implement `clearValue()` if clearing means more than `value = ''`.

The error text the field shows: the consumer's `error-text` while `error` is set, else an
error the control found itself, else the validation message once it should show.

members.name: fieldAria
members.description: Attributes for the native control: name, invalid state and description, plus `configAria`.

members.name: renderField
members.description: Renders the `wc-field` frame around `control`, plus the hidden description.

members.name: emitValue
members.description: Dispatches `input` or `change` with the current value, the field event contract.

members.name: clearValue
members.description: Clears the value for the clear button. Fields with other empty values override it.

members.name: handleFieldFocus
members.description: Tracks focus of the inner control; bind to its `focus` and `blur`.

members.name: fieldDescription
members.description: The text the description carries: the error, else the warning, else the help.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Label shown above the field; also the control's accessible name.

attributes.name: placeholder
attributes.description: Hint shown inside the empty control.

attributes.name: helper-text
attributes.description: Help text shown below the field.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Shows the field in its error state with `error-text`.

attributes.name: error-text
attributes.description: Error message shown below the field while `error` is set; replaces the help text.

attributes.name: warning
attributes.description: Shows the field in its warning state with `warning-text`.

attributes.name: warning-text
attributes.description: Warning message shown below the field while `warning` is set; replaces the help text.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Visual variant of the field.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Height of the field: `sm` (2.5rem, default), `md` (3.5rem) or `lg` (4rem).

attributes.name: clearable
attributes.description: Shows a button that clears the value while the field has one.

attributes.name: configAria
attributes.description: ARIA attributes moved from the host onto the inner control.
